title: Which exponent rule does each part need?
description: Five parts are simplified and written in exponential form, using the same exponent rules as the worked example in the book. A power of a power and a bracket with two letters need their own steps, and a number check confirms one part.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose the exponent rule from what happens to the powers in each part, then work with the exponents. Watch for students who add the exponents in a division, or who give only one letter in the bracket its exponent.

video_script.why: A learner picks the right exponent rule for each part, the same way as the worked example on simplifying powers.
video_script.substitution: the book's own five parts: two negative exponents, two divisions, a power of a power and a bracket with two letters
video_script.anchor: five parts with powers written in a column on the board
video_script.payoff_line: Each part needs one exponent rule: add, take away, or multiply

final_answer.value: (i) 10 to the power −7 (ii) 5³ (iii) 9 to the power −11 (iv) 13 to the power 6 (v) m to the power 14 n to the power 21
final_answer.spoken: part one, ten to the power negative seven; part two, five cubed; part three, nine to the power negative eleven; part four, thirteen to the power six; part five, em to the power fourteen, en to the power twenty one

video_script.design: One idea: choose the rule from the operation, then work with the exponents. Each part sits on its own line and the letter answer only appears at the answer; a number check closes the working.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; five parts (i) to (v) in a column with a question mark

marks.one: (i) 10^-2 x 10^-5 is written in the column
marks.five: (v) m^5 n^12 (mn)^9 is written in the column
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the column

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Simplify ten to the power negative two times ten to the power negative five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Then five to the power seven divided by five to the power four.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Then nine to the power negative seven divided by nine to the power four.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Then thirteen to the power negative two, all to the power negative three.
<bookmark mark='five'/>The last has em to the power five and en to the power twelve. It also has em en, all to the power nine.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each answer in exponential form.

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: rule cards: same base times, add the exponents; same base divided, take the exponents away

marks.same: the worked example from the book is set beside the five parts
marks.add: two rule cards open: times adds the exponents, divided takes them away
marks.pick: each part is matched to one card

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Times means add the exponents, and divided means take them away.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>We pick the rule for each part separately.

marks.given: the five parts are written in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five parts, each with powers to simplify.

beats.on_screen: To find: each part in exponential form

marks.find: the words each part in exponential form are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each part as one power, in exponential form.

marks.same: the same base 10 is circled in both powers
marks.add: -2 + (-5) = -7 is written in the exponent, giving 10^-7

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, in part one the bases are the same and the powers are multiplied.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add the exponents. Negative two plus negative five is negative seven.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, parts two and three divide powers of one base, so we take the exponents away. Seven take away four is three.
<bookmark mark='three'/>In part three, negative seven take away four is negative eleven.

marks.pow: (13^-2)^-3 is written, a power of a power
marks.mul: (-2) x (-3) = 6 is written in the exponent, giving 13^6

narration: <bookmark mark='pow'/>Step three, part four is a power of a power. For this, the two exponents are multiplied.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Negative two times negative three is positive six, so the result is thirteen to the power six.

marks.add: 5 + 9 and 12 + 9 are written in the exponents of m and n

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step four, part five has a bracket. The bracket gives em to the power nine and en to the power nine.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Each letter now has two powers. Five plus nine is fourteen, and twelve plus nine is twenty one.

marks.same: 78125 / 625 = 125 = 5^3 is written and matches part two

narration: <bookmark mark='big'/>Step five, check part two with numbers. Five to the power seven is seventy eight thousand one hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Five to the power four is six hundred and twenty five. Dividing gives one hundred and twenty five, which is five cubed.

marks.pay: the rule used in each part is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Each part needs one exponent rule: add, take away, or multiply.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Part one is ten to the power negative seven, and part two is five cubed.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Part three is nine to the power negative eleven, and part four is thirteen to the power six.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Part five is em to the power fourteen, en to the power twenty one.
